observations.detail: Full-disk SDO/AIA 193 Å image at 2026-10-25 03:27:53 UT shows active regions, coronal loops, and dark coronal holes.
Maximum Kp over last 24 h is 3.0 (quiet to unsettled).
Forecast max until 2026-10-25 12:56 UTC is None; no NOAA geomagnetic scales are currently in effect.
Alert ALTEF3: flux exceeded 1,000 pfu; yesterday maximum 3,169 pfu on 2026-10-23 at 1540 UTC.
Kp=4 threshold reached 2026-10-23 1953 UTC; warning was valid 2026-10-23 1926 to 2026-10-24 0900 UTC.
A single AIA 193 Å image cannot confirm an Earth-directed CME.

assessment.risk_reasoning: Kp is currently low (3.0) with no active geomagnetic storm scales and no forecast storm indicated. Elevated relativistic electron flux primarily raises satellite charging concerns, not neutral-density drag. No Earth-directed CME is confirmed. Absent a CME impact or sustained Kp ≥ 5, thermospheric density over LEO should remain near climatological levels.

trace.policy_text: Manoeuvre when Pc >= 1e-4 and a verified option exists. Between 1e-5 and 1e-4, or when Pc is diluted, prefer getting precise data if there is time before the latest safe burn. On public TLE data, do not decide a burn while there is time to get precise ephemeris; TLE screening finds candidates, it does not decide manoeuvres. Never manoeuvre if our propulsion status is unverified. If the other object is an active satellite that can manoeuvre, contact its operator before moving; if it is an operational satellite whose capability is unknown, notify its operator. Keep at least 30 minutes for command upload. Max 1.0 m/s per burn.

decision.rationale: Pc exceeds the 1e-4 maneuver threshold, our satellite has verified propulsion capability, the other object is non-maneuverable debris, burn option O1 provides the required miss distance with minimal delta‑v and ample lead time for command upload, and space weather conditions are nominal.
